name_note: The GTDB species Prevotella copri_M is one of several narrow species-level clades split out of the classical Prevotella copri, whose genomes carry the NCBI name Segatella copri; published findings below refer to Segatella copri or to the wider complex, not to this clade alone.

sentences.text: Segatella copri, formerly named Prevotella copri, is a common human gut microbe that has been both positively and negatively associated with host health.
A cross-continent meta-analysis of more than 6,500 metagenomes reported that Prevotella copri encompasses four distinct clades, nearly ubiquitous and co-present in non-Westernized populations.
A later study combining targeted isolation with metagenomic analysis defined 13 Segatella copri-related species, nine of which are present in humans and differ in prevalence across populations.
That work reported associations between members of the complex and male sex, and positive correlations with lower visceral fat and favourable markers of cardiometabolic health.
A survey of 76 adults from eight tribal communities in India reported Segatella copri dominant at mean 25 to 47 percent relative abundance.
